limitations: I/B/E/S ACTU_EPSUS has no actual-level primary/diluted company-basis flag. Baseline therefore uses a disclosed basic/primary approximation (EPSPXQ and primary OPEPSQ), applies no unsupported annual dilution factor, and never infers basis from estimate-level PDF or value proximity. ACTU PENDS is period-end YYYYMM precision, so matching is at ticker/year/month; candidate mappings to multiple Compustat DATADATEs in the same month are excluded as ambiguous.

Future quarterly CFO/FCF per-share flows are rebased to the initial-quarter share basis with the relative Compustat AJEXQ_t/AJEXQ_k factor. This relies on Compustat’s current cumulative factor history; the ratio removes any common terminal base. The paper does not explicitly describe split rebasing for its future-flow sum, so this is a provider-supported best-effort interpretation of its per-share construction.

The physical p. 11 statement that there is “still only one firm observation per calendar quarter” appears in the return-test discussion. It is applied to the full-sample cash-flow panel by retaining the latest DATADATE among matched reports within each firm/calendar quarter before horizon eligibility; its scope for the cash-flow tests is not completely explicit.

Quarterly item #108/#90 mnemonic mapping is semantic best effort because the local catalog does not preserve the paper-vintage numeric crosswalk; current OANCFY/CAPXY YTD semantics are provider-verified.

Pooled 1st/99th percentiles and within-quarter OLS are best-effort choices where the paper is silent. The printed footnote 9 omits the usual factor of 2 in the Newey–West variance multiplier; xtfmb uses standard Newey–West inference. Only individual coefficient t-statistics are used.
